questions.q:
From the given options, identify the sentence which is in the positive degree.

(SSC MTS 2024 S.51_05-Nov_Shift-1)
o: His brother is an intelligent boy.
I have a greater idea in this regard.
They are playing hockey with longer sticks.
She is the most beautiful girl of the class.
questions.s:
Answer: a) His brother is an intelligent boy.

Explanation:
The positive degree is the base form of an adjective, used when no comparison is being made.

  • "Intelligent" is in the positive degree → simply describes without comparing (बिना तुलना के गुण बताना)

  • "Greater" = comparative degree (तुलनात्मक)

  • "Longer" = comparative degree

  • "Most beautiful" = superlative degree (सर्वोत्कृष्ट)

Only option (a) uses the adjective in the positive degree.

questions.q:
The mountain lion is / one of the slyest and more / elusive animals in the woods.

[MTS-13/07/2022 S1]
o: one of the slyest and more
questions.s: In this sentence, there is an issue with the usage of "more" with the superlative "slyest." The word "more" is unnecessary and grammatically incorrect when used with a superlative adjective. The correct structure should be: "one of the slyest and most elusive animals.”

questions.q:
When it started raining, I ran to the nearer house for shelter.

[CGL Tier-1-06/03/2020 S1]
questions.s: "Nearer" is used for comparing two things, while "nearest" is used for one thing. Since only one house is being referred to, "nearest" is the correct answer.

questions.q: This is (a) / the more beautiful (b) / painting in the collection. (c) / No error (d)

among all the singers.

"He received the best employee award because he was the m̲o̲r̲e̲ ̲h̲a̲r̲d̲w̲o̲r̲k̲i̲n̲g̲."

  • When comparing one person as the top in a group, we use the superlative form of the adjective.

  • "Hardworking" is a two-syllable adjective that commonly forms the superlative with "most" rather than "-est".

  • Hardworking – positive form, no comparison

Correct sentence:

questions.s: "most luminous" is incorrect here. The correct form should be "more luminous" because we're comparing the brightness of stars to the Sun, and "more" is used for comparative adjectives.

questions.q:
Match the following:

A. Beautifuli. Superlative degree
B. Smartestii. Comparative degree
C. More handsomeiii. Positive degree
questions.s:
Most adjectives form their comparatives by the addition of - r or - er, and their superlative by the addition of - st or - est (depending on the spelling) to the positive. Here, the suffix 'est' has been used with the word 'smart' making it a superlative degree.

In some cases, adjectives (usually having more than two syllables in the spelling) form their comparative by using the adverb more with the positive, and the superlative by using the adverb most with the positive. Here 'more' has been used with the word 'handsome'. So, it forms a comparative degree.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.s:
The given sentence indicates a comparison between two sisters. So, a comparative degree of adjective will be used. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The final sentence will be: She is richer than her sister.
